articles.full_summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials investigates the comparative cardiovascular outcomes and safety profiles of GLP-1 RAs in type 2 diabetes.
articles.key_finding: In adults with T2DM, GLP-1 RAs as a class reduce the risk of MACE by approximately 14% with an acceptable safety profile, supporting their role as a cornerstone of cardiovascular risk reduction.

articles.title: Cardiovascular and Kidney Outcomes and Mortality With Long-Acting Injectable and Oral Glucagon-Like Peptide 1 Receptor Agonists in Individuals With Type 2 Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Trials.
articles.snippet: Lee MMY, Sattar N, Pop-Busui R, Deanfield J, Emerson SS, Inzucchi SE et al. | Diabetes care | 2025-May-01 | Journal Article; Systematic Review; Meta-Analysis
articles.full_summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 10 randomized trials found that long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonists, including both injectable and oral formulations, reduce the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), hospitalization for heart failure (HHF), kidney events, and all-cause mortality in individuals with type 2 diabetes.
articles.key_finding: Across 10 trials (n = 71,351), long-acting GLP-1RA reduced incidence rate of MACE by 14% (HR 0.86 [95% CI 0.81, 0.90]; I2 = 27.6%), HHF by 14% (0.86 [0.79, 0.93]; I2 = 2.1%), and the composite kidney outcome by 17% (0.83 [0.75, 0.92]; I2 = 20.4%) and all-cause mortality by 12% (0.88 [0.82, 0.93]; I2 = 17.5%).

response.global_summary:
Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) significantly reduce major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and all-cause mortality in adults with type 2 diabetes [0][1][4][5][8][9]. Multiple meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials consistently report a reduction in MACE ranging from **10% to 14%** [0][1][4][6][7][9]. Specifically, a 2026 meta-analysis found a **14%** reduction in MACE for GLP-1 RAs as a class [0]. Other meta-analyses reported similar reductions: a 2025 meta-analysis of 67,769 participants with type 2 diabetes found a **13%** reduction in MACE [1], while another 2025 meta-analysis across 21 trials and 99,599 patients reported a **13%** reduction in MACE (IRR: **0.87**) [5]. A 2018 meta-analysis of adult patients with type 2 diabetes showed a **10%** relative risk reduction in the three-point MACE outcome [4].

Beyond MACE, GLP-1 RAs also reduce the risk of all-cause death and cardiovascular death. A 2025 meta-analysis of 85,373 participants, including 67,769 with type 2 diabetes, found a **12%** reduction in all-cause death (HR **0.88**) [1]. Another 2025 meta-analysis of 99,599 patients reported a **12%** reduction in all-cause death (IRR: **0.88**) and a **13%** reduction in cardiovascular death (IRR: **0.87**) [5]. A 2025 meta-analysis focusing on long-acting GLP-1 RAs in 71,351 individuals with type 2 diabetes also found a **12%** reduction in all-cause mortality [9]. A 2018 meta-analysis specifically noted a **13%** relative risk reduction in cardiovascular mortality [4].

GLP-1 RAs have also been shown to reduce specific cardiovascular events. A 2025 meta-analysis, which included patients with and without type 2 diabetes and/or prior atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), found that GLP-1 RAs reduced the risk of total myocardial infarction (MI) by **14%** (RR: **0.86**) [2]. Large randomized cardiovascular outcomes trials have consistently demonstrated that several GLP-1 RAs reduce events such as myocardial infarction, stroke, cardiovascular death, and heart failure [3]. A 2020 meta-analysis observed a non-statistical trend toward a reduction in heart failure (MH-OR **0.93**) [8]. The reduction in MACE by GLP-1 RAs appears consistent across subgroups of patients with and without established cardiovascular disease, with meta-analyses in 2019 and 2021 reporting non-significant heterogeneity between these subgroups [6][7].

In addition to cardiovascular benefits, GLP-1 RAs also demonstrate positive effects on kidney outcomes. A 2025 meta-analysis of 67,769 participants with type 2 diabetes showed an **18%** reduction in the composite kidney outcome and a **16%** reduction in kidney failure [1]. Similarly, a 2025 meta-analysis of long-acting GLP-1 RAs in individuals with type 2 diabetes found a **17%** reduction in the composite kidney outcome [9]. The safety profile of GLP-1 RAs is considered acceptable [0]. A 2020 meta-analysis found that GLP-1 RAs did not increase the risk of atrial fibrillation [8].

key_findings.text: GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) significantly reduce the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in adults with type 2 diabetes by approximately 10% to 14%.
GLP-1 RAs reduce all-cause mortality by 12% and cardiovascular death by 13% in patients with type 2 diabetes.
GLP-1 RAs reduce the risk of total myocardial infarction by 14%, including in patients with and without type 2 diabetes and/or prior atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.
GLP-1 RAs reduce the composite kidney outcome by 17-18% and kidney failure by 16% in individuals with type 2 diabetes.
The reduction in MACE with GLP-1 RAs is consistent across subgroups of patients with and without established cardiovascular disease.
GLP-1 RAs do not increase the risk of atrial fibrillation.

evidence_gaps: The sources do not provide specific details on the comparative efficacy or safety profiles of individual GLP-1 RA drugs for cardiovascular risk reduction.
The sources do not extensively detail the long-term safety profile beyond the reported trial durations, nor do they specify potential adverse events beyond atrial fibrillation.
